TrickWork comes as a Flatpak for Linux, wears a new shield logo and follows GlimStone 4.3.6. The Version card names the right version again.

## ✨ Added

- TrickWork comes as a Flatpak for Linux too, for x64 and ARM64. It brings its own WebKitGTK and opens and saves files through your desktop's own dialogs, so it sees only the folders you pick there. Flatpak looks after its updates, so Update automatically stays off there and says why, and Check for updates points you to your software centre. The README, the docs and the App card in the container all offer the download.
- An OLED switch under Theme puts the dark theme on true black for OLED and AMOLED screens. It belongs to the screen you use, so it stays on this device. With Light chosen it can't be flipped and says why.
- The first swatch under Accent can take your system's colour: the accent of Windows, macOS or Linux in the desktop app, and in Firefox or Safari the colour your system gives the browser. A wand marks it, and TrickWork follows when you change the colour in your system's settings.

## 🎨 Design

- TrickWork has a new logo, a shield with a hash sign. You'll find it in the README, in the header, as the favicon and as the app icon on Windows, macOS, Linux and in the Flatpak.
- The look follows GlimStone 4.3.6.
- A row of choices stays on one line at every width. Where its words don't fit, as on a phone, it shows its symbols alone and names each one in its bubble. The Settings tabs and the Labels choices do this on a narrow screen.
- While you drag a card, the other cards tremble and the one in your hand holds still under the pointer.
- Check for updates wears two circling arrows.
- The ARM, Portable and Flatpak ARM parts of the download buttons on the App card show one word and no second line.
- A grey button takes a touch of the accent when you point at it or reach it with the keyboard, and under rainbow every button lights up in a colour of its own.

## 🐛 Fixed

- 1.6.1 still called itself 1.6.0 inside the app. The Version card showed 1.6.0, Check for updates kept offering 1.6.1, and the download buttons on the App card fetched the files of 1.6.0. The app now carries the version it is released as, and a test makes sure it stays that way.
